- Session: `session_01BaTeBCjaoTDmDWFVmSY2jL`

- Worktree: `../objectstack-7750` (dedicated)
- File surface: `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/my-work.page.ts` — the fix is one word, `filters:` → `filter:`.

**The one-word fix is not the interesting part; the verification bound is, and the dispatch requires it stated honestly rather than papered over.** objectui#4041 (`9154d9e`) retired the plural spelling and pinned that the declared `filter` reaches `$filter` — but it landed **after** the console pin this run served (`09987b680`), so on a console built at the old pin `filter` was not yet a reachable declared input. End-to-end verification therefore depends on the vendored `packages/console/dist` being rebuilt (#7752).

So the dev checks which pin the worktree vendors: if it carries `9154d9e`, drive the page and show `$filter` on the wire before and after. If it does not, ⛔ **no fabricated end-to-end claim and ⛔ no rebuilding the vendored console to manufacture one** — report the bound, pin what is checkable inside this repo, and reference #7752.

**Premise re-verification required before implementing:** that line 52 still reads `filters:` on current `main`, and that `filters` really does appear **exactly once** across the showcase while every other page uses `filter`. If other sites exist, the card is under-scoped and that is worth knowing before one line is changed.

**Scope, carried verbatim so nobody over-escalates it:** ⛔ this is **not** an authorization bypass — the unfiltered read is still RLS-constrained and the caller sees only rows they may see. The defect is that a *declared personal-scope filter silently never applies*. ⛔ Not to be relabelled as a security fix.

**⛔ #7751 is out of scope** — the general problem (a typo'd key accepted without complaint) is the larger card and is filed separately. Not folded in, and no validation added to the block schema here.

**ACCEPT** — patch verified, PR #7764 flipped ready, auto-merge armed.

The patch is what I asked for and slightly better. Rather than reword one shared string, you split the shared assertion into per-key `{ key, why }` pairs so each spelling carries its own reason, and the new JSDoc states the distinction outright — `filters` is **DEAD** (zero read points, dropped before the wire), `defaultFilters` is **ALIVE** (the legacy path `object-grid` still reads and lowers to `$filter`, pinned absent because this page authors the *current* key, not because the legacy one is inert). The added warning is the part that will actually do work later: a future author debugging a filter bug must not read this test as licence to treat `defaultFilters` as a no-op **nor reach for it as a workaround**. Both failure directions, named.

Confirmed the constraints held: the page fix is byte-identical, no assertion's truth value changed, and the diff is still the same two files.

**Your correction to the card's "exactly once" sub-claim stands as the record.** `filters` appears at three other authored sites in the showcase, all legitimate declared plural keys on other surfaces (`ObjectNavItem.filters`, react-tier `ListView.filters`). The card is correctly scoped, but not for the reason it gave — read literally the claim is false, read as *"exactly one `object-grid` authors the plural"* it holds. Reporting that instead of quietly smoothing it over is what let it become useful downstream.

**And it was useful downstream.** I routed the vocabulary-drift finding to #7751 rather than opening a twin, with all three of its claims verified against `origin/main` first. I also added the consequence you didn't state, which changes what closing #7751 costs: `validate-component-props.ts`'s skip of unregistered types is **deliberate and load-bearing** — its own header says so, and turning it off would fail 87 legitimate nodes. So the hole is upstream of the lint rule, in SDUI block props not being knowable to this repo's linter, and the existing `optionsSource` alias machinery only helps once they are.

**The verification bound was the right call and I want it on record as such.** `packages/console/dist/` is gitignored and absent from a fresh clone, so no run in this repo can show `$filter` on the wire until #7752 lands. You measured what *was* checkable — the pin ancestry, via `compare/9154d9e...6314e87f2` returning `status: ahead, behind_by: 0` — and declined to manufacture the rest. A fabricated end-to-end claim here would have been worth less than no claim, because it would have retired the card while leaving the actual gap unmeasured.

Changeset skip independently re-verified: `@objectstack/example-showcase` is `private: true` and appears zero times in the `fixed` group.
